questions.q: On a dashboard with a fixed running user, what data does every viewer see?
options: Only the records they personally own
Whatever the running user is allowed to see
Nothing until they refresh
Only public records
questions.explain: With a fixed running user, everyone sees the data that user can access, regardless of their own permissions.

options: It refreshes itself every minute
It has more than 10 widgets
Its running user is always the person viewing it
It can only be opened on mobile
questions.explain: In a dynamic dashboard, the running user is the logged-in viewer, so each person sees data according to their own access.

questions.q: Which scenario best suits a dynamic dashboard?
options: A 'My Pipeline' dashboard used by many reps and managers
A wall display showing one identical company scoreboard
A dashboard that must be emailed on a fixed schedule
A dashboard with no filters
questions.explain: Dynamic dashboards let different people see different slices from a single dashboard, ideal for personal or team pipeline views.

questions.q: What is a common limitation of dynamic dashboards mentioned in this lesson?
options: They cannot include charts
They generally cannot be refreshed on a schedule the way fixed-user dashboards can
They only work in Classic
They cannot use filters
questions.explain: Because there is no single user to refresh as, scheduled refresh is generally unavailable for dynamic dashboards, and editions also cap how many you can have.

questions.q: Why is choosing a fixed running user a security consideration?
options: It deletes records from the org
It changes the profile of every viewer
It can expose records that the running user can see to viewers who otherwise could not
It disables field-level security for the whole org
questions.explain: Viewers see the running user's data view, so sensitive records visible to the running user may be visible to everyone with dashboard access.
